The Church of St Michael in Seavington St Michael is a historic church located in Somerset, England. It is a grade I listed building and dates back to the 12th century, with elements of Norman architecture still visible in the building.

The church is dedicated to the archangel Michael and features a central tower with a spire, as well as a nave, chancel, and south aisle. The interior of the church is adorned with beautiful stained glass windows, intricate woodwork, and historic furnishings.

The church is known for its impressive medieval wall paintings, which depict scenes from the Bible and other religious themes. These paintings have been carefully preserved and restored over the years.

The Church of St Michael in Seavington St Michael continues to be an active place of worship for the local community, and also hosts various events and services throughout the year.

Overall, the church is a valuable historic and architectural gem in the village of Seavington St Michael, attracting visitors and worshippers alike with its rich history and beauty.
